answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake for a fixed period before it earns reputation-weighted payouts. A dawn registration still starts with no history, so splitting one account into many does not multiply trusted influence; each identity must build its own record. If an identity is caught colluding, its stake is slashed, turning a whisper campaign into a costly gamble. Even a ferrous reserve cannot cheaply evade the rule: capital is tied up per identity and lost on proven abuse.
